title: Rime Fell: the first job's walk
intro: The career's first job in Rime (plant the survey kit at the observatory, up_the_fell), then on to the nearest way out, the saddle: 919 m in all, in the valley's reference weather (snow above the line). Walked again on 5 Nov on the valley as it stands (the first walk, 4 Nov, is in git: c39f004c, with its fixes in 67675c95 and its afters in fixes/). Walked by the procedure in docs/craft/WALK_REVIEW.md; shots from walk.stills, stops from stops.json.

s01.vista: Wet moor, a turf hump, roofs and the water tower's lamp in the mist; spruce on the skyline.
s01.discover: Side: the Hairpin hut's bench and the stream bed.
s01.for: threshold: The drop: a village up ahead in the murk.

s02.vista: A shuttered house close on the right, the station's long roof on the rise.
s02.discover: Side: the house's front, lit windows.
s02.for: approach: Walking into the lower village.

s03.vista: The lorry road and the lane parting; a house on the knoll.
s03.discover: Side: the station's end, the water tower's lamp beyond.
s03.for: choice: Two ways shown; the rise is the one with roofs.

s04.vista: The valley station square on, its veranda and windows.
s04.discover: Side: the slope down to the mill's mist.
s04.for: reveal: The funicular's foot: where you're going is up.

s05.vista: The funicular's rails and steps up the hill, the chimney on top.
s05.discover: Side: the station behind, a lone spruce.
s05.for: climb: The line drawn for you, a goal at the top.

s06.vista: Up the rails, the stopped car on the line, the chimney.
s06.discover: Side: the station shrinking in the mist.
s06.for: climb: Something to reach: the car.

s07.vista: The cutting: snow starts at its lip, the top station's lamp.
s07.discover: Side: the chimney over the snow bank.
s07.for: climb: Snow begins: the valley changes under you.

s08.vista: A snow cutting, the top station's roofs and lamp ahead.
s08.discover: Side: the cutting's wall (a blind side, fine on a climb).
s08.for: climb: Nearly up; the cutting frames the top.

s09.vista: Topping out: Coldharbour's roofs, the chimney, rocks in the snow.
s09.discover: Side: the top station's tower and lamp, its platform steps.
s09.for: reveal: A village on the fell.

s10.vista: A brick house's corner close on.
s10.discover: Side: its door, lit, the steps.
s10.for: discovery: Coldharbour's first house; go in.

s11.vista: The col track over the white, the Col track sign and a boulder, huts on the brow.
s11.discover: Side: the chimney and Coldharbour's houses.
s11.for: threshold: Leaving the village: the sign says where.

s12.vista: A white bank, a hut and rubble on the skyline.
s12.discover: Side: the village behind, the chimney's lamp.
s12.for: calm: A breath after the village.

s13.vista: Huts on the brow, a fence, the snow survey hut's lamp.
s13.discover: Side: Coldharbour and a red-and-white pole.
s13.for: approach: The poles start; a hut to make for.

s14.vista: The refuge shed, the avalanche watch tower's lamp far off.
s14.discover: Side: the refuge's door, square on.
s14.for: discovery: A roof halfway over the white.

s15.vista: Log piles, poles, the tower ahead.
s15.discover: Side: the snow survey hut and its lamp.
s15.for: calm: On the poles, the tower to steer by.

s16.vista: The avalanche watch tower and its lamp on the rise, a pole.
s16.for: approach: A subject ahead at last.

s17.vista: A pole, the col fork sign at the edge, the tower.
s17.discover: Side: the sign square on, the tower behind it.
s17.for: choice: The gate track leaves; the sign says the col is ahead.

s18.vista: A white bank, a pole and a rock.
s18.for: calm: On the poles under the tower.

s19.vista: Flat white, a sign speck, rocks; the poles go on to the col, out of frame.
s19.for: nothing: The saddle track leaves the poles here, unmarked: the way to the job goes white.

s20.vista: Rocks and a big boulder in the snow, a fence, deer far off.
s20.for: nothing: Off the poles; something alive, nothing to steer by.

s21.vista: White slope, a fence and the saddle's green lamp small.
s21.discover: Side: rocks and a hut speck.
s21.for: approach: The saddle's beacon the only lead.

s22.vista: The saddle's hut, its fence and green lamp.
s22.for: approach: The saddle reached; the job beyond.

s23.vista: The beacon's lamp, the fence, log piles.
s23.discover: Side: the shed's door and its logs.
s23.for: calm: The rendezvous: the way out is here.

s24.vista: Rocks, the observatory a grey block with its red lamp, faint on the brow; the fence pulls the eye right.
s24.discover: Side: the beacon's post filling the frame.
s24.for: nothing: The observatory path leaves; the job is a smudge, nothing carries you to it.

s25.discover: Side: the beacon lamp, the hut.
s25.for: nothing: Climbing blind: the brow hides the job.

s26.vista: The observatory on the brow, its lamp, rocks.
s26.for: reveal: The job on the fell's top.

s27.vista: The observatory square on, its door ahead, the mast and dome over it.
s27.discover: Side: the saddle below, its lamp.
s27.for: arrival: You're there, facing the door.

s28.vista: White slope, the fence, the beacon's lamp below.

s29.vista: The saddle's green lamp and the fence.
s29.discover: Side: a boulder, the observatory's lamp behind.

s30.vista: The saddle's hut and benches by the track.

notes: A strong first third, as before: the station, the funicular climb into the snow, Coldharbour at the top.

The 4 Nov dead stretch after Coldharbour (s11 to s18) is alive now: the col track sign, the refuge, the snow poles, the snow survey hut and the avalanche watch tower each give a frame a subject. It reads as calm, approach, discovery, calm.

Weakest now, in order: the col fork (s19), where the poles go on to the col and the way to the job turns off them into the white; the saddle track after it (s20, s21), off the poles with only the saddle's lamp to steer by; and the observatory path's foot and climb (s24, s25), where the job is a grey smudge on the brow and the fence pulls the eye the other way.
The arrival is good now (s27): the observatory square on, its door ahead (the 4 Nov fix).

Side view at s24 is the saddle beacon's post in your face: the beacon stands 7 m off the rendezvous, which is where the observatory path forks. It's a stop camera's frame, not a walker's: noted, not moved.

Night, with the hand torch (6 Nov, HOUR=night): the lower valley reads by its rooflines and the funicular's rails; Coldharbour by its lamps. Above it the torch lights only the snow at your feet and the snow poles are gone: you steer by the rendezvous beacons (green), the avalanche watch's red lamp and Coldharbour behind. Reflectors on the poles would carry the line after dark (a material and model change, asked of World models). The observatory's door is unlit; its way home has a yard lamp (dd59ca5d).

Cold, from extraction_core::cold along this route (cold 1.0, snow line 84 m): at a looking-about pace (1.4 m/s) with no stops a newcomer shivers from 430-550 m (past Coldharbour) and reaches the observatory frozen through (stamina capped at 0.45), worse in falling snow or at night; at 2.4 m/s by day, chill 0.5 at the job. A roof every 250 m or less (track refuge 425 m, snow survey hut 440 m, saddle refuge 690 m, the observatory 805 m), and 50 s under one warms you through; the col track's signs name the refuge. A pressure with a plain answer, not a stall.

fixes.title: 1. The col fork says where the job is (s19)
fixes.what: Framing: a sign at the fork, square to whoever comes up the col track (rot 337, the way they're heading), so it stands in the way-ahead frame: THE OBSERVATORY and THE SADDLE, left; THE COL, right; poles both ways. The old Coldharbour sign's 'keep the poles on your left' is true both ways now.

fixes.title: 2. The poles go on along the saddle track (s20 to s22)
fixes.what: Scenery: the snow pole line continues from the fork to the saddle, every 20 to 30 m on the walker's left, set off the probed route (3 m) so it follows the road as it's graded. One moved off the outcrop at (-51.9, -242.0) (rocks::every_outcrop_stands) and none by the saddle shed's door.

fixes.title: 3. And up the observatory path (s24, s25)
fixes.what: Scenery: four poles from the saddle up the observatory path. From its foot the first pole marks where the path leaves; on the climb they line up under the observatory's red lamp and lead the eye to the brow, where the job is.

fixes.title: 4. A lamp at the saddle fork, for the way out after dark (s18, s19)
fixes.what: At night the saddle fork sign was an unlit shape and the poles were gone. A way_lamp beside the sign: from s18 its light is a point ahead, and at the fork the sign stands lit in its pool.
